title: Canonical coefficient-change pullback and adjoint comparisons
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$. For coefficient families $R,S$ and a compatible change $a:R\to S$ [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data], use the actual derived scalar extension and its restriction adjunction [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower] and the ordinary geometric module adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], [def-sp-open-coefficient-adjunction-data]. Define scalarPull to be the left-adjoint uniqueness comparison whose right-adjoint comparison is the canonical scalar-restriction/direct-image square. Define properComparison as the inverse scalar-adjunction mate of the inverse of that square [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; define openComparison as the inverse scalar-adjunction mate of the open-unit-normalized restriction square. For a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], define reduction by the completed coefficient projection, finiteQuotientChange by the canonical quotient maps for all $1\leq n\leq m$, and completedChange by the finite-extension inclusion on completed coefficient sheaves. At positive finite level, define finitePullbackIso by uniqueness of left adjoints from the equality of the normalized direct images and the specified intrinsic module adjunction [def-sp-finite-intrinsic-direct-adjunction]; define finiteOpenIso by uniqueness of open left adjoints using that pullback comparison [def-sp-finite-intrinsic-open-square]. These are definitions of maps, not assertions of their invertibility or coefficient preservation beyond the isomorphisms explicitly built by uniqueness.
